messages:
sasha: heads-up — quick RFC follow-up re: tiling/affinity boundaries for policy runtime. posted notes and a rough sim in the repo, want feedback.

ria: saw it briefly. main worry is cross-tenant affinity creating sticky shards that block hotfallbacks.

kevin: can you link the sim? also curious how tiling impacts probe latency.

sasha: link: https://git.internal/routing/sim/tiling-2026

marco: TL;DR of the sim numbers? i can't open this now.

sasha: TL;DR: with 4x tile width we get 12% cost drop for stable workloads, but 2x latency p50 increase under bursty probes. tradeoff: fewer KV cache evictions vs longer decision time.

ria: that's expected. question: can we split affinity metadata into 'soft' vs 'hard' so runtime can ignore soft when under latency SLO pressure?

kevin: +1. soft/hard split sounds good but need clear API between policy engine and runtime. runtime needs a quick path: prefer -> don't-block -> fallback.

sasha: proposal in RFC: policy returns a tuple (preferred_routes[], hard_constraints[]) where preferred_routes are hints the runtime can ignore under time budget. hard_constraints are non-negotiable.

marco: how does this interact with region-tiering? e.g., customer pins region=eu as soft preference but SLA wants lat<100ms.

sasha: runtime should run constraint checker first (hard_constraints) then apply preferred_routes only if decision_time budget remains. fallback to global-compatible model if not.

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary policy compile pass on staging (tiling-slimdown) — 6/6 hosts ok :white_check_mark:

ria: also we need telemetry: tag decisions with 'honored_hint' vs 'dropped_hint' + reason to tune tiling width automatically.

kevin: agree. also add counters for 'fallback_due_to_time_budget' and 'fallback_due_to_capacity'.

sasha: I'll update RFC with API sketch and add a minimal proto: ```json
{"preferred_routes": ["r1","r2"], "hard_constraints": ["region:eu","latency:<200ms"]}
```

marco: can we avoid shipping full preferred_routes list for big selectors? maybe provide a compact fingerprint + async resolution?

sasha: yes — include an optional 'selector_fingerprint' that runtime can resolve via async lookup to avoid big payloads.

ria: looks good. action items?

kevin: 1) sasha update RFC, 2) eng-runtime to implement quick-path checker + honor budget, 3) observability add tags/counters, 4) simulate tiling widths with mixed workloads.

sasha: filing tasks now. thanks all.
